h: A film, then the full Skeggy works
p: Skegness is a town that does its best business on sunny days, which is exactly why a cinema in the middle of it is so handy. When the North Sea wind picks up or the rain sets in, Tower Cinema on Lumley Road gives you a couple of hours of dry, comfy entertainment without needing to get back in the car. Lumley Road is the main shopping street, running down towards the famous Clock Tower, so you're right in the thick of things the moment you come out.

A good plan with kids is to book a screening for the middle of the day, when they're most likely to be flagging or the weather's at its worst, then hit the seafront afterwards. Pack a few wet wipes for sticky popcorn fingers and check the film's certificate if you've got a mix of ages in tow.
Fitting it into a seaside day

From the Clock Tower, the seafront opens up in both directions. Grand Parade is lined with the bright, noisy amusements Skegness is famous for, the pier stretches out towards the sea and the beach is a huge, sandy playground at low tide. Natureland Seal Sanctuary along the North Parade is a favourite with families, and the Embassy Theatre on the front hosts shows through the year.

If you've got a few days, Fantasy Island up the road at Ingoldmells is another big draw, and quieter stretches of coast such as Gibraltar Point nature reserve, to the south of town, give you dunes, saltmarsh and birdwatching when you fancy a break from the bright lights. Skeggy is all about mixing and matching, and a film slots nicely in between the chips and the candy floss.
Remember the access note above if anyone in your group can't manage stairs, and have a back-up plan for them, as the town has plenty of step-free attractions along the front.
